data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network of small, independently operated services can be MORE resilient to correlated failure than one large service with strictly more internal redundancy, provided the dominant failure mode is control-plane coordination rather than individual component failure. The strict total-redundancy advantage of the monolith is a red herring when failures are governed by central misconfiguration or coordination collapse.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Failures are dominated by component-level wear-out rather than control-plane decisions, in which case the monolith's strict redundancy advantage dominates.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The decentralized services are operationally homogeneous (e.g., all using the same cloud provider or same deploy tooling), collapsing the independence of the control planes and recreating monolithic correlated risk.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The monolith architecturally isolates its redundant components across independent control planes internally (e.g., via strict cell-based architecture), negating the decentralization advantage.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Large monolithic services concentrate control over all redundant components in a single control plane. A single logical error (e.g., a bad deploy, a centralized misconfiguration, or a shared dependency update) can simultaneously disable all internally redundant paths, making the mathematical redundancy moot. In a decentralized network, redundant capacity is partitioned across independent control planes (different teams, deploy schedules, and operational practices). A fault originating in one control plane is bounded and cannot propagate across the entire system's redundancy. Thus, even with strictly less total component redundancy, the decentralized network survives correlated control-plane faults the monolith cannot.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
